messages.content: Use web search to find relevant datasets. Only include landing pages or DOIs. Do not invent links. Do not call time, date, timestamp, or clock tools.

Query: Can you find datasets about Political behaviour and attitudes in Germany during the 2020s?
Respond ONLY as JSON in this exact shape: {"items":[{"title":"...","url_or_doi":"...","justification":"..."}]}. Put any DOI, URL, landing page, or link in url_or_doi.

queries: GESIS GLES German Longitudinal Election Study 2021 2025 datasets
GESIS ALLBUS 2021 2023 2025 Germany political attitudes dataset
Germany political attitudes 2020 2024 dataset European Social Survey Germany
German election study 2024 2025 political behavior panel dataset GESIS
action.query: GESIS GLES German Longitudinal Election Study 2021 2025 datasets

content.text: {"items":[{"title":"German Longitudinal Election Study (GLES) – Federal Elections 2021 and 2025","url_or_doi":"https://www.gesis.org/en/gles/data-and-documentation","justification":"One of the most comprehensive datasets on political behaviour and attitudes in Germany. Includes voting behaviour, party identification, political preferences, ideological orientations, political trust, and electoral participation. The 2021 and 2025 federal election studies provide cross-sectional and longitudinal survey data, making them particularly suitable for analysing political change during the 2020s."},{"title":"GLES Cross-Section 2025 – Post-Election Survey","url_or_doi":"https://search.gesis.org/research_data/ZA10100","justification":"Provides individual-level survey data collected following Germany's 2025 federal election. Covers electoral choices, political attitudes, party preferences, and evaluations of political actors. Particularly useful for studying recent voting behaviour, political polarisation, and changes in electoral support."},{"title":"GLES Panel – 2024–2025 Federal Election","url_or_doi":"https://www.gesis.org/en/gles/2025-federal-election","justification":"Longitudinal panel surveys following German voters before and during the 2025 federal election. Enables researchers to investigate changes in political attitudes, voting intentions, party identification, and electoral decision-making at the individual level."},{"title":"GLES Tracking Surveys 2009–2026 – Cumulative Dataset","url_or_doi":"https://search.gesis.org/research_data/ZA6832","justification":"A cumulative collection of repeated surveys examining political opinions and electoral preferences in Germany. Includes observations throughout the 2020s, allowing researchers to investigate changes in party support, political trust, ideological positioning, and political issue priorities over time."},{"title":"German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) – 2021, 2023 and 2025","url_or_doi":"https://www.gesis.org/en/allbus/data-and-documentation","justification":"A nationally representative social survey covering German residents' political attitudes, social values, institutional trust, ideological orientations, and social characteristics. The 2021, 2023, and 2025 waves are particularly relevant for studying changes in political attitudes during the 2020s and their relationships with demographic and socioeconomic factors."},{"title":"ALLBUS 2023 – German General Social Survey","url_or_doi":"https://www.gesis.org/en/allbus","justification":"Provides survey data on social and political attitudes in Germany in 2023. Includes questions concerning political decision-making, democratic values, social inequality, and political orientations. Particularly useful for analysing political attitudes in the post-pandemic period and comparing them across population groups."},{"title":"ALLBUS Cumulative Dataset 1980–2023","url_or_doi":"https://www.gesis.org/en/allbus/data-and-documentation","justification":"Combines multiple waves of the German General Social Survey into a harmonised dataset. Allows researchers to compare political attitudes observed during the 2020s with earlier decades, making it suitable for analysing long-term changes in political trust, democratic orientations, and ideological preferences."},{"title":"Politbarometer – German Political Opinion Surveys","url_or_doi":"https://search.gesis.org/?study_group=Politbarometer&type=research_data","justification":"A collection of recurring public opinion surveys examining German political attitudes and electoral preferences. Covers voting intentions, party evaluations, satisfaction with government performance, democracy satisfaction, political interest, and perceptions of major political issues. Surveys from 2020 onward are particularly useful for analysing short-term fluctuations in political opinion."},{"title":"GESIS Election Studies – German Federal and State Elections","url_or_doi":"https://www.gesis.org/en/services/finding-and-accessing-data/election-studies","justification":"A research data collection containing survey datasets on German federal and state elections, including elections held during the 2020s. Provides information on electoral participation, voting intentions, political preferences, and evaluations of political parties. Particularly valuable for comparing political behaviour across German regions and election cycles."},{"title":"GLES Rolling Cross-Section – German Federal Election 2025","url_or_doi":"https://www.gesis.org/en/gles/2025-federal-election","justification":"Part of the German Longitudinal Election Study's 2025 election programme. Designed to investigate electoral attitudes and preferences during the election campaign. Particularly useful for studying campaign dynamics, changes in voting intentions, political issue salience, and the relationship between political events and voter preferences."},{"title":"GLES Candidate Study – German Federal Election 2025","url_or_doi":"https://www.gesis.org/en/gles/2025-federal-election","justification":"Provides survey information about candidates participating in Germany's 2025 federal election. Relevant for studying political elites' ideological orientations, policy positions, political priorities, and candidate characteristics. Can be combined with voter surveys to investigate differences between political representatives and citizens."},{"title":"GLES Panel 2024 – Profile Wave A5","url_or_doi":"https://www.gesis.org/en/gles/2025-federal-election","justification":"A panel survey wave conducted in 2024 as part of the GLES longitudinal research programme. Provides individual-level information about political preferences and attitudes before the 2025 federal election. Useful for examining the stability of party identification, political attitudes, and electoral preferences over time."}]}
